ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MRS. JUSTICE SUNITA AGARWAL)
1.

The present petition has been filed by the legal heir of Daduji Bhavaji, who was original owner of the land-in-question and in whose name, the award dated 9.1.1995 under Section 11 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was passed.

2. It seems that reference application dated 25.7.2014 has been filed by the petitioner herein,

1 namely Rehmatkhan Daduji Malek, to seek enhancement of compensation under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contention in the writ petitioner that the notice, prior to making of the award, was not served and the petitioner had received the certified copy of the award on 13.6.2014 and, hence, the reference application filed by the petitioner within the period of limitation, is wholly misconceived.

It is not permitted for the legal heir of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/4192/2024 ORDER DATED: 15/03/2024 undefined original owner to assert that the notice was not served on his predecessor, inasmuch as, there was no occasion for serving of the notice upon the petitioner during the lifetime of his predecessor.
The date of death of the predecessor-in- interest of the petitioner herein, namely the original owner of the land-in- question, in whose name the award was made, has also not been disclosed.

3. For the aforesaid, we do not find any merit in the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner to issue directions to the respondent authority to refer the matter to the competent Court under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act.
In any case, it appears that the original owner did not assail the award during his lifetime and it is not permitted to his heir to file reference.
The writ petition is, thus, found misconceived and hence, DISMISSED.

Sd/-
(SUNITA AGARWAL, CJ ) Sd/-
